text:
kevin: FYI weve got a customer in private-endpoints beta seeing ~30% packet loss for responses to requests that enter via their VPC endpoint and are routed back via peering. symptoms look like asymmetric routing / reply packets taking a different path and getting dropped.

kevin: quick repro traces attached below (trimmed):

```
# from customer pod -> endpoint
traceroute to 10.200.0.10 (10.200.0.10), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.3.1  0.2 ms  0.1 ms  0.1 ms
 2  100.64.5.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
# response path seen on our relay host
# reply src 10.200.0.10 dst 10.0.3.5 -> next-hop in diff AZ
ip route get 10.0.3.5 from 10.200.0.10
  via 100.64.9.2 dev eth0  src 10.200.0.10 uid 0
```

anya: do we know if the reply path crosses an extra NAT or different routing table? looks like the endpoint host picks a next-hop based on its route table (AZ-local route missing).

omar: customer topology is dual-homed: they have a primary peering route to our regional relay and a fallback direct-peering to another account. replies are sometimes egressing via fallback region where theres no return-route to the source ENI, hence RSTs/drops.

sarah: this is the usual asymmetric routing headache with shared egress. two high-level ways to fix: preserve source ip (so replies come back to same place) or pin return path (ensure routing decision symmetric).

kevin: brainstormed options:
- short-term: implement return-path pinning at controlplane: attach a local route for the tenant ENI on the endpoint host so replies prefer the same interface that accepted the packet. cheap but adds per-tenant route churn.
- short-term alternate: SNAT at endpoint host to a stable per-tenant egress IP (preserve continuity). easier but breaks original source IP visibility for customers.
- med-term: per-tenant ENI / per-tenant secondary IP allocation so source IP always maps to same physical host and route table. more infra cost but clean.
- long-term: BGP-like route advertisement from endpoint hosts to peering routers so route resolution is symmetric (requires peering controller work and cross-account route programming).

anya: tradeoffs: per-tenant route programming means we need to scale iptables/iproute entries and have fast GC. SNAT is simpler but will require us to expose XFF handling and update billing/monitoring.

omar: also need to consider cross-account security groups & route table limits. some customers already close to the max routes for per-VPC peering.

sarah: could we do a hybrid: for customers who opt-in to IP-preservation SLA we provision per-tenant ENI; for others use SNAT. that reduces blast radius and gives product choice.

kevin: operational concerns: if we do per-tenant route pinning we must avoid controlplane storms on mass attach/detach. need a rate-limited reconciler and batching of route writes. also add metric: "asymmetric-replies" counted on endpoint host (conntrack misses / RSTs)

infra-bot: deploy-bot: test-job asymmetric-routing-gate rolled to staging; added conntrack metrics to endpoint host canary.

anya: proposed immediate actions:
- kevin: prototype local return-path pinning with small LRU table (store src cidr -> accept-iface) + metric, deploy to staging.
- omar: run capacity check for per-tenant route entries and list customers near VPC route limits.
- sarah: draft a short product note outlining SNAT tradeoffs and opt-in ENI SLA so customer success can discuss with impacted customers.

kevin: timeline: prototype in staging this week, gather conntrack/dropped reply metrics for 48h, converge on plan (SNAT vs ENI) next architecture sync.

omar: one more idea: could use a small dataplane shim that proxies downlink for a small number of tenants (egress minions). cheap to scale horizontally and keeps src IP if we proxy the flow, but adds latency and another hop. note for eval.

kevin: agreed. ill include proxy minion evaluation in the prototype notes. thanks all. will post staging link & graphs here once available.
